candidates.title: FlowMoDE: Coarse-to-fine Flow Matching for Detail-aware Sim-to-Real Monocular Depth Estimation
candidates.abstract: Monocular depth estimation is a fundamental capability for 3D spatial perception in robotic and intelligent systems. While data-driven discriminative methods have achieved compelling performance for monocular depth estimation, generative approaches can reconstruct fine structural details with stronger generalization. However, most existing generative diffusion models suffer from low inference efficiency caused by multi-step sampling, whereas single-step diffusion models struggle to recover high-fidelity depth maps. To mitigate these drawbacks, this paper presents FlowMoDE, a coarse-to-fine flow-matching-based framework for efficient, structure-aware monocular depth estimation supporting sim-to-real and cross-scene generalization. The core architecture first conducts coarse-level decoding conditioned on diffused features extracted from a pre-trained semantic encoder, and subsequently restores fine-grained structural patterns via expanded decoding layers. Trained exclusively on a single synthetic indoor dataset, our proposed method outperforms prior methods across five real-world indoor and outdoor datasets, yielding an average 14.1% reduction in relative error against state-of-the-art works as well as 9.9\% reduction in chamfer distance for point cloud reconstruction. We further validate the generalization capability of FlowMoDE on realistic robotic scenes, with qualitative comparisons against state-of-the-art methods. The project page is https://flowmode-shao.netlify.app/

candidates.title: SACQ: Structure-Aware Codebook Quantization for Ultra-Low-Bit Vision-Language-Action Models
candidates.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models enable capable robot behavior, but their large memory footprint limits deployment on resource-constrained robotic platforms. Weight quantization is a natural remedy, yet post-training quantization (PTQ) recipes inherited from large language models degrade when applied to VLAs at ultra-low precision. Existing low-bit PTQ methods often fail to explicitly account for the structure of downstream operations and allocate precision without considering its effect on the policy actions. We introduce SACQ, an ultra- low-bit weight-only vector-codebook quantization framework for VLAs. SACQ combines (1) structure-aware codebook fitting with role-specific quadratic metrics that reflect input statistics and downstream sensitivity; (2) action-aware mixed-bit allocation based on the increase in final-action error as individual layers are compressed; and (3) two-stage post-quantization refinement that reassigns codeword indices with second-order error compensation and calibrates codebooks and row-group scales against the decoded action. Using GR00T N1.7, SACQ achieves 93.85% average success across four LIBERO suites at 1.5 bits per language/action weight while reducing model memory by 4.83x. With INT8 activation quantization and low-precision attention, it retains 93.55% success while running 1.51x faster than BF16. On SimplER, SACQ further achieves 63.76% and 52.27% success under Visual Matching and Variant Aggregation at 2 bits per language/action weight, compared to 58.90% and 53.45% for BF16, respectively.

candidates.title: DrawSplat: Atlanta World-Guided Implicit Gaussian SLAM for Indoor Reconstruction
candidates.abstract: RGB-D SLAM requires accurate online tracking, high-quality rendering, and geometrically consistent reconstruction. Existing Gaussian SLAM methods mainly optimize Gaussian primitives with photometric, depth, or local frame-to-model constraints, which are often insufficient in indoor scenes with weak textures, large planar structures, noisy depth, and long trajectories. The resulting maps may suffer from pose drift, surface thickness artifacts, noisy normals, and blurred structural boundaries. We propose DrawSplat, an Atlanta World-guided implicit Gaussian SLAM framework for indoor reconstruction. DrawSplat follows a drawing-like process: explicit point-line geometry first sketches the structural layout, and implicit neural Gaussians then fill in high-fidelity appearance and continuous geometric details. It estimates camera poses, sparse geometry, and gravity direction through point-line joint tracking, infers structural planes from tracked lines using the shared-gravity component of the Atlanta World prior, and converts them into differentiable regularization terms on Gaussian centers and normals. To improve compactness and efficiency, DrawSplat further combines an anchor-based implicit neural Gaussian representation with adaptive structural sampling, which allocates Gaussian capacity to structurally informative regions. Experiments on multiple datasets show that DrawSplat achieves robust tracking, high-fidelity rendering, and strong geometric reconstruction among Gaussian-based SLAM systems, while maintaining a practical balance among quality, efficiency, and model size.

candidates.title: REA: A Routed Embodied Agent Runtime for Asynchronous Brain-Cerebellum Control
candidates.abstract: Foundation models are becoming remarkably reliable at high-level reasoning, yet they remain too slow and costly to serve as fine-grained controllers. Conversely, fast policies like VLAs and whole-body controllers offer more efficient reflexes, but struggle to generalize. While pairing a deliberative brain (foundation models) with a reactive cerebellum (fast policies) seems natural for embodied systems, two obstacles remain: methods are built and scored on incompatible stacks, and their asynchronous coordination is difficult. For example, an agent that calls the VLA in the agentic loop can stall the fast execution, while a VLA that calls the agent on errors tends to re-trigger fallbacks repeatedly or completely miss silent failures. To address this, we propose REA (Routed Embodied Agent), a unified runtime where a deliberative System 2, an embodied router System 1 and reactive System 0 policies cooperate under a single golden rule - no running policy waits on the brain. Instead of querying the brain at each failure, REA employs a route memory that stores each policy's measured success ahead of time, a boundary-triggered judge gate that consults the brain on policy execution, and a shared-budget escalation ladder for bounded recovery. Evaluated on 3,000 test episodes across 60 LIBERO-Pro tasks, REA reaches 95.9% success and beats the best single-agent baseline in its own policy pool (94.7%) while reducing control steps by 25% and control time by 17%. In a separate 100-episode RoboTwin 2.0 study, REA achieves 84% success with VLA policies and 86% with VLA+code, compared with 80% for the strongest single VLA baseline MEDex. These results demonstrate learned and programmatic policies operating within the same runtime. REA also transfers to BEHAVIOR-1K and a real Unitree G1 humanoid, achieving the highest observed success among the compared methods.

candidates.title: VoxLution: Evolving Voxels for High-Fidelity 3D Scene Generation
candidates.abstract: High-resolution 3D indoor scene generation is crucial for immersive applications such as virtual reality, spatial computing, and robotics simulation. We introduce VoxLution, a coarse-to-fine transformer-based approach that generates high-fidelity indoor scenes with rich details, overcoming the overly smooth geometry typical of existing generative models. First, we generate a low-resolution spatial layout; then, based on this structural information, we progressively refine the scene geometry locally in chunks. Key to our approach is formulating 3D super-resolution as a sequence modeling problem over multi-resolution sparse voxel grids. To achieve this, we introduce a training-free, resolution-invariant tokenization scheme that compactly encodes the geometric information of eight octants into a single decimal number. We formulate the transformer sequence to include multiple resolutions, allowing the coarse layout to guide the generation of fine local details. To ensure coherence across local chunks, we incorporate adjacent chunk boundary information directly into the transformer sequencing. VoxLution achieves scene generation at a finer voxel resolution than existing baselines, demonstrating state-of-the-art performance on standard benchmarks with 59.6% lower FPD and 51.1% lower FID on 3D-FRONT, and 70.5% lower FPD and 73.8% lower FID on Scannet++.

candidates.title: DyCraft: An Agentic System for Long-Horizon 4D Scene Generation
candidates.abstract: While frontier coding agents can generate high-quality 3D scenes and articulated assets, they struggle to create coherent long-horizon animations. When equipped with general-purpose harnesses, they frequently produce physically implausible outputs, generating objects that interpenetrate, lack physical support, or move unnaturally. Such bare agents struggle to repair these errors because they default to scripting the full animation in one pass, making it difficult to verify their work and disentangle complex spatiotemporal constraints. Drawing on the practice of human animators, we introduce DyCraft, a system for animated 3D scene generation that breaks animation into steps that coding agents can more reliably solve. DyCraft first expands the user's prompt into a detailed plan and builds a static scene. It then creates a 3D storyboard of key animation poses, where each frame is a static 3D scene that the agent can build and debug in isolation. Storyboarding decomposes the problem into pairs of verified start and end states, allowing the agent to author local motion between them with a collection of motion authoring tools. We evaluate DyCraft on 24 long-horizon, multi-shot animation tasks covering humanoid robots, human and animal characters, and physical mechanisms. Compared with a native GPT-6 agent in Codex and prior agentic baselines, DyCraft substantially reduces physical violations and generates higher-quality animated 3D scenes that are more often preferred by human raters.

candidates.title: EgoHSI3R: Online 4D Hand-Scene Interaction Reconstruction from Egocentric Video
candidates.abstract: Egocentric videos offer an abundant source of hand-scene interactions for embodied learning, which requires recovering hands, camera, and scene consistently in a shared 3D world. Existing methods focus on either camera-frame hands or world-space hand trajectories, without jointly recovering the scene pointmaps or interaction information. Building a complete reconstruction from such specialized predictions therefore typically requires per-sequence optimization. We propose EgoHSI3R, a unified feed-forward framework for online 4D hand-scene interaction reconstruction from egocentric monocular video. To jointly recover these components, it maintains a recurrent scene representation that accumulates geometric evidence over time and provides a shared world space and scale. We introduce hand-centric prompts that fuse pretrained hand priors and local scene context, while MANO vertex queries attend to scene features to predict dense per-vertex contact. These designs enable a single network to jointly estimate camera motion, dense scene geometry, world-space bilateral MANO hands, and per-vertex hand contact. Despite operating causally, EgoHSI3R achieves the lowest world-space hand joint error on ARCTIC among the evaluated methods, while offering faster inference than existing world-space hand reconstruction pipelines and competitive camera and scene reconstruction accuracy.

candidates.title: Prior-Guided Single-Exposure HDR Novel View Synthesis via Base-Gain Representation
candidates.abstract: Single-exposure high dynamic range (HDR) novel view synthesis (NVS) recovers HDR scenes from low dynamic range (LDR) views captured at a single exposure and estimates camera response function (CRF) for LDR re-exposure. Without HDR ground-truth, using single-exposure LDR views as the sole source of direct supervision underconstrains HDR reconstruction and cannot ensure its faithful recovery, motivating the need for learned LDR-to-HDR reconstruction priors. Moreover, single-exposure LDR views supervise CRF only over a limited range, necessitating a learnable prior for reliable re-exposure beyond it. We propose PriorGS, a 3D Gaussian Splatting framework that addresses both challenges by (1) guiding HDR recovery with pseudo-HDR supervision from 2D single-exposure HDR reconstruction methods while anchoring it to input LDR views through a closed reconstruction loop; and (2) regularizing CRF modeling with a learnable prior that guarantees monotonicity and promotes plausible responses. Yet cross-view inconsistencies in independently generated pseudo-HDR targets impair scene reconstruction when HDR is encoded directly as Gaussian's color attribute. We therefore introduce a 3D base-gain HDR representation that factors HDR radiance into an LDR base and an overlaid 3D gain field, promoting robustness to such inconsistencies and enabling 3D HDR appearance editing. Extensive experiments demonstrate PriorGS's substantial superiority over baselines.

candidates.title: TRACE: Target-State Risk-Aligned Conditional Execution for Embodied Tracking
candidates.abstract: Embodied visual tracking requires a robot to follow a language-specified person under occlusion, look-alike distractors, and ambiguous instructions. We show that improving tracking persistence can simultaneously increase safety violations. Using a compact 0.6B vision-language-action (VLA) tracker with a frozen backbone, we update only the planner head with proximal policy optimization (PPO). PPO improves success and following rates across all three EVT-Bench settings, but increases the collision rate on distracted tracking because episodes that previously ended in target loss can instead end in contact. We introduce TRACE, an execution-time target-state risk gate that preserves the learned policy and intervenes selectively. A lightweight risk head processes 84 cues, including candidate boxes, identity margins, a learned range-and-bearing probe, and the policy's commands. When the calibrated risk exceeds a threshold, TRACE rescales the translational component of the next waypoint while leaving yaw unchanged. The executed action is identical to PPO's on more than 98% of steps. In paired evaluations on identical episodes, TRACE reduces the distracted-tracking collision rate by 3.96 percentage points, while further improving success and following rates. Matched slowdown controls without target-state timing do not reproduce this improvement. Concurrent evaluation reproduces a collision reduction of 3.77 points, compared with 0.29 points for identical-arm null pairs, indicating that the effect exceeds evaluation variability. These results show that target-state-aware execution can recover the safety cost of policy post-training with minimal intervention.

candidates.title: When the Past Shapes Action: Understanding Embodied Memory
candidates.abstract: Recent advances in generative foundation models have expanded the capabilities of embodied AI, enabling increasingly general navigation, manipulation, and long-horizon task execution. However, effective interaction with dynamic environments requires more than only strong perception and reasoning: agents must act with partial knowledge and retain, retrieve, and update information from past observations, actions, and experiences. This survey examines embodied memory as a mechanism for preserving decision-relevant information beyond the current observation. We organize existing approaches along two complementary dimensions: six fundamental memory requirements, spanning world-state persistence, task progress, belief maintenance, and experiential learning; and eight architectural categories, including recurrent states, fast weights, visual and symbolic representations, spatial memory, and experience-based systems. We analyze their capabilities and limitations, and examine how existing benchmarks evaluate memory-dependent behavior, distinguishing genuine use of historical information from general task performance. Finally, we identify open challenges in selecting relevant experiences, maintaining consistent beliefs in changing environments, and consolidating knowledge across episodes. Our analysis provides a framework for understanding memory as an essential component of reliable, adaptive, and lifelong-horizon embodied intelligence.

candidates.title: Visual-Inertial RGB-D SLAM with Encoders for a Differential Wheeled Robot
candidates.abstract: Recent years have seen multiple impressive results in visual-inertial odometry (VIO) techniques, by which accurate state estimation can be achieved via the extended Kalman filter (EKF) or nonlinear optimization. However, these approaches are rarely open source, and they tend to fail in real experiments due to the temporary lack of feature points and fast motion. Therefore, in this study, we used encoders to overcome the temporary failure of purely vision-based simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM). Here, we propose a generative measurement model for encoders and derive an expression for the maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimate and necessary Jacobians for optimization. We use our theory to present a novel tightly coupled visual-inertial encoder RGB-Depth (RGB-D) SLAM system. Tests on our system on an in-house dataset confirmed that our modeling effort led to accurate (with a root mean squared error (RMSE) of approximately 2-7 cm) and robust state estimation in real time. The source code and our dataset containing the encoder information have been published for verification.

candidates.title: Sensorium: An Open-Source Multimodal Data Collection and Curation Library for Embodied Surgical AI
candidates.abstract: Embodied surgical AI requires reliable multimodal data, yet surgical data collection remains costly, difficult to repeat, and strongly dependent on the hardware setup. We present Sensorium, an open-source Python library for recording, processing, annotating, and curating multimodal surgical data from configurable robot and sensor streams using the Robot Operating System (ROS) and ROS2 middleware. The library combines operator-facing data acquisition, configurable processing, semantic annotation, and episodic dataset generation. We evaluate Sensorium across 1516 recordings of phantom, ex vivo, and in vivo porcine experiments involving multiple surgical tasks and sensing configurations, and report preliminary usability feedback.

candidates.title: A Capability-Aware Backup-Recoverability Filter for Heterogeneous Multi-Robot Navigation
candidates.abstract: Safe navigation in heterogeneous multi-robot teams faces two coupled challenges: differences in robots' braking and turning capabilities limit how each robot can respond to an approaching neighbor, while simultaneous interactions require a single control action to satisfy multiple collision-avoidance constraints. Together, these challenges can make local safety constraints incompatible with a robot's admissible controls, leaving a decentralized safety controller without a feasible action. We propose a Capability-Aware Backup-Recoverability Filter (CA-BRF), based on the insight that navigation actions should preserve access to a certified recovery maneuver. First, we construct a backup-recoverable set in a shared Cartesian operational space by evaluating whether prescribed backup maneuvers maintain pairwise safety until the robots come to rest. Each maneuver respects the corresponding robot's kinematic and actuation constraints, making the recovery certificate capability-dependent. Second, CA-BRF filters candidate controls by selecting admissible interpolations between candidate and backup actions while coordinating the selection across simultaneous interactions. This preserves backup recoverability while retaining as much of the candidate action as possible and ensures that all pairwise recovery conditions are satisfied by a single executable control for each robot. Together, we establish recursive feasibility and safety for the discrete-time closed-loop system even when the nominal safety-constrained optimization becomes infeasible. The validity and effectiveness of the proposed CA-BRF are validated in simulations with up to 30 heterogeneous robots and experiments of robots with five different kinematic classes.

candidates.title: AC-SMPC: Differentiable Actor--Critic MPC with State Constraints for Safe and Fast Robot Navigation
candidates.abstract: Achieving safe navigation in confined dynamic environments remains a challenging problem, as robots must balance navigation efficiency with safety. Existing actor--critic MPC architectures typically employ differentiable MPC layers, but this way cannot readily accommodate explicit state constraints, making it intractable to involve collision avoidance within learning-based planning. To address this issue, we propose an actor--critic model predictive control framework with state constraints. We first use vertices to represent the robot and obstacles, and half-spaces to represent the workspace. Based on these, the nonlinear robot dynamics is locally linearized and the hyperplane-based collision avoidance constraints are convexified into the differentiable MPC layer, and then the actor exploits closed-loop feedback to adjust the MPC objective parameters that shape local motion behavior, while the critic evaluates long-term task performance. We further relax the convexified constraints with bounded and penalized slack variables to form an elastic quadratic program, accommodating cases where the local constraint approximations cannot be satisfied simultaneously. Simulation tests and experiments, involving dynamic collision avoidance for multi-robot in narrow cases, illustrate the advantages of the proposed framework in adaptively adjusting the learned policy and improving navigation efficiency over existing approaches while maintaining the motion safety.

candidates.title: Robot Navigation and Canine Welfare: A Pilot Study Surfacing Challenges for Cross-Species Legibility and Proxy Validity in Animal-Machine Interaction
candidates.abstract: Autonomous delivery robots increasingly share residential spaces with companion animals, yet navigation behavior is rarely designed with animal welfare in mind. This paper presents a pilot study evaluating a curve-out maneuver, a laterally arcing pass-by trajectory triggered at the dog's alert distance, proposed as a candidate welfare-informed navigation intervention grounded in canine social communication research and legible motion theory. Following a research through design approach, we developed and evaluated a first design iteration of the artifact in a naturalistic home environment with a companion dog. Contrary to our hypothesis, the curve-out produced a more acute stress response than the straight-line baseline. We argue that discontinuous execution limitation, the robot stopping and reorienting multiple times to approximate the arc, undermined legibility, which in itself became a stressor. The pilot surfaces the legibility of robot behavior to non-humans' eyes and proxy stimulus validity as structural challenges for AMI and repositions the design problem for future work.

candidates.title: WorldBridge: Bridging Video and Action for Task Generalization in World Action Models
candidates.abstract: Achieving the broad task generalization of embodied models in physical environments remains a central challenge in robot learning. We study this challenge in World Action Models (WAMs) through two complementary capabilities: video generalization, which predicts the visual evolution of new tasks, and action generalization, which translates these predictions into executable behavior through a video-to-action bridge. By varying video and action supervision for tasks outside an initial training set, we examine their respective contributions to task transfer. On RoboTwin 2.0, using only in-distribution video-action supervision yields a 25.07% success rate on out-of-distribution tasks. Introducing videos of these tasks without their action labels raises success to 55.90%, while adding just one action-labeled demonstration per task further improves it to 70.70%. These findings suggest that broader video coverage enables task transfer by leveraging existing inverse-dynamics capabilities, while even sparse action supervision further strengthens those capabilities. Guided by this perspective, we introduce WorldBridge, a WAM with separate video and action experts connected through structured attention and trained with joint flow matching. WorldBridge incorporates visual memory at two temporal scales and action forcing, alongside a unified data processing pipeline that standardizes and filters heterogeneous robot trajectories and egocentric hand-derived supervision. Across multiple manipulation benchmarks, WorldBridge achieves state-of-the-art performance among the compared methods, including 96.23% on RoboTwin 2.0 full data setting and 80.9% on clean to random setting, 82.8% on RoboCasa GR1 TableTop, and 57.6% on DOMINO Level-1. Our study highlights the complementary roles of video prediction and action grounding in developing robots that generalize across tasks.

candidates.title: TalkFlow: Structured Latent Flow Matching for Speech Driven Holistic Motion Generation
candidates.abstract: Holistic co-speech motion generation aims to synthesize coordinated facial expressions, hand gestures, and body movements from speech, which is challenging due to heterogeneous part-specific dynamics, long-range temporal coherence, and cross-part coordination. Directly modeling high-dimensional motion can be unstable, while overly compact or unstructured latent spaces may lose fine-grained motion details. We present \textbf{TalkFlow}, a structured latent flow framework for speech-driven holistic motion generation. TalkFlow learns a continuous three-stream latent representation for upper-body motion, lower-body motion, and facial expressions, preserving part-specific dynamics without forcing heterogeneous motion components into a single latent space. To maintain holistic coordination, lightweight cross-stream interactions are incorporated in both latent representation learning and flow-based generation. Conditioned on multi-level speech features, TalkFlow performs speech-conditioned latent flow matching, learning a continuous transport process from source latents to realistic motion latents. Experiments on the BEAT2 dataset demonstrate strong performance across facial expression accuracy, body gesture quality, and speech-motion synchronization. Qualitative comparisons and user studies further show that TalkFlow generates more natural, expressive, and speech-aligned holistic motion than state-of-the-art methods. The project page is available at https://xinmuwang.github.io/TalkFlow/.

candidates.title: Dynamic Skinning: Kinematics-Driven Cartoon Effects for Articulated Characters
candidates.abstract: We present an extension to traditional rig skinning, like Linear Blend Skinning (LBS), to produce secondary motions that exhibit the appearance of physical phenomena without need for simulation. At the core of the technique, we call dynamic skinning, is a set of deformers which offset position of individual vertices as a function of position derivatives and time. Examples of such deformers create effects such as oscillation in response to movement and the appearance of wave propagation, among others. Because the technique computes offsets directly and does not solve physics equations, it is extremely fast to compute. It also boasts a high degree of customizability which supports a desirable artist workflow and fine level of control. Finally, we showcase the technique in a number of scenarios and make comparisons with the state of the art.

candidates.title: SemEllipsoid: Semantic-aware Shape Abstraction with Ellipsoid
candidates.abstract: Representing 3D shapes using a set of primitives - known as shape abstraction - is an actively studied problem in computer graphics with wide applications in shape understanding, analysis, and simulation due to the compactness and computational efficiency of the primitive-based representation. Prior work has primarily focused on geometry-aware shape abstraction, where the objective is to approximate the input shape with a minimal set of primitives while preserving geometric fidelity. However, these methods often overlook semantic consistency, inevitably leading to primitives that span across multiple semantic parts. Such inconsistency can cause undesirable artifacts in downstream tasks such as part-level shape editing or manipulation. In this paper, we introduce a new task - semantic-aware shape abstraction, where the goal is to produce abstractions that are both geometrically faithful and semantically consistent, ensuring that each primitive adheres strictly to a single semantic part without crossing semantic boundaries. We propose SemEllipsoid, a novel method to address this problem using ellipsoidal primitives. The core idea is to inject semantic constraints into the primitive optimization process leveraging the availability of semantic cues from large-scale foundation models. We design a fully differentiable projection-blending-evaluation scheme to measure semantic divergence against input semantic masks, and formulate an alternating optimization strategy to iteratively solve for optimal semantic assignment and primitive configurations. Our method is non-learning-based, requiring no data collection or network training, and generalizes well to shapes from arbitrary categories. It also supports different levels of abstraction according to user demand. Extensive experiments and evaluations validate the effectiveness of our approach across several 3D shape collections.

candidates.title: Altered Visual Hand Feedback in Virtual Reality: An Exploratory Study in Essential Tremor
candidates.abstract: Pathological tremor is the most prevalent movement disorder worldwide, characterized by involuntary muscular oscillations within a frequency of 3 to 12 Hz. Despite extensive research, the underlying mechanisms that generate and modulate tremor are not yet understood, and treatments are usually insufficient. While it is known that visual feedback is an important afferent pathway, little is known about the impact of altering the hand's visual representation on tremor expression. With the development of immersive technologies, VR poses an excellent tool to study how alterations to the representation of the hands affect tremor. In this work, we study this through two complementary experiments. In the first one, we show that a consumer-level hand-tracking system substantially attenuates tremor-band movements without preventing successful task completion. In the second one, with eight patients with essential tremor, we observe task-dependent differences in physical tremor between VR and the real world, with several patients exhibiting lower tremor-band activity in both hand kinematics and muscle oscillations, particularly during reaching tasks. Our findings represent an initial step toward validating the use of VR as an experimental tool for the research and treatment of pathological tremor, while highlighting strong user- and task-dependent effects.

candidates.title: From Teleoperation to Long-Horizon Dexterity: Evaluating Visuomotor Skills and Offline Proxies for Dexterous Manipulation
candidates.abstract: Imitation learning policies are intended to make robotic manipulation robust to variations in object pose, appearance, and environment that challenge pre-programmed motion. However, real-world performance remains difficult to predict, as conventional optimization signals such as validation loss show no consistent relationship with robot success. To identify the design choices that govern real-world performance, 281 imitation-learning policies spanning seven policy families were evaluated in approximately 1,700 real-robot trials of RJ45 connector grasping and insertion using a five-fingered robotic hand. Controlled ablations showed that observation and action representations dominated conventional optimizer and sampling choices. For point-cloud policies, region-of-interest cropping, representation in the robot-base frame, and normalization within the point encoder each improved success by 70-100 percentage points. For the vision-language-action policy, absolute rather than relative action prediction improved insertion success by up to 70 percentage points. Skill decomposition, multi-view perception, and recovery demonstrations were associated with the strongest-performing systems, although their effects were not independently isolated. Of 67 offline metrics evaluated, only five measures of predicted-motion smoothness and directness reliably correlated with insertion success (r = -0.70 to -0.80), and only within a single policy family. These results identify representation choices as key determinants of real-world imitation-learning performance and show that offline metrics can shortlist policies, but cannot replace real-robot evaluation.

candidates.title: STAR: Steering Action Representations during Inference
candidates.abstract: Vision-language-action models (VLAs) map language instructions and visual observations to robot actions, showing strong capabilities across robotic manipulation tasks. However, in our probing experiment, we find that action representations near the action output do not fully preserve task-relevant visual grounding. Motivated by this late-layer grounding gap, we introduce STAR, for STeering Action Representations, a training-free inference method for pre-trained VLAs. STAR applies an exponential moving average over late-layer residual updates, allowing later action representations to inherit object-aware update directions from earlier layers without model updates or architectural changes. It further uses recent proprioceptive states to adapt the mixing strength, using conservative mixing when execution dynamics change rapidly. Experiments on robot manipulation benchmarks show that STAR improves late-layer object awareness and increases average task success rates by 4.0 percentage points. Our code is available at https://github.com/PKU-VaLuE-Lab/STAR.

candidates.title: QUAL: Quantile Alignment Improves Zero-Shot Time-Series Foundation Models
candidates.abstract: Time-series foundation models (TSFMs) provide zero-shot forecasts for unseen series, but their accuracy varies across datasets. Combining several models can reduce this variability, yet zero-shot deployment provides no target labels for selecting or weighting them. We find that a model pool is useful not only as a final ensemble, but also as a probability reference for transforming each member forecast. Aligning quantiles through this pool-relative reference improves every member forecast in aggregate. Motivated by this finding, we propose QUAL (Quantile alignment), a simple label-free framework for improving and combining diverse TSFMs. QUAL first produces aligned member forecasts, then applies Huber aggregation and rearrangement to obtain a robust combined forecast without training or model modification. On GIFT-Eval, quantile alignment reduces average member MASE and CRPS by 7.4% and 9.8%. The full framework remains robust when weak forecasters enter a candidate pool whose quality cannot be verified in advance. Code is available at https://github.com/junhyeokkang/QUAL.

candidates.title: FrontierMat: Benchmarking Language Models at the Frontier of Materials R&D
candidates.abstract: To accelerate materials discovery, language models must be able to address problems at the research frontier. Yet textbook- and examination-derived benchmarks primarily assess established knowledge, leaving performance on frontier research problems largely untested. We introduce FrontierMat, a benchmark of 330 problems drawn from frontier academic and industrial research in fields including aerospace, semiconductors, embodied intelligence and nuclear fusion. Every problem is validated by leading experimentalists and industry experts in its field. Each problem presents a real study and asks the model to infer a withheld outcome or draw a conclusion from selected experimental evidence. Problems are annotated by functional domain, material system and the scale of the governing mechanism; 130 require cross-scale reasoning. The strongest general-purpose model scores only 53.7%, and on matched problems, cross-scale problems score 8.7 points below single-scale ones. Half of the problems are solved by at most one model, and models fail chiefly by endorsing what is plausible rather than what was observed. A domain-adaptation study with meta-weighted continued pretraining and scale-modular self-distillation raises an open-weight model from 36.7% to 55.4%, matching the strongest proprietary model, with improvements on public materials benchmarks and no decline in aggregate performance on general benchmarks. FrontierMat provides a testbed for measuring progress toward language models that support frontier materials R&D.

candidates.title: VLA Policies Do Not Know When Not to Act: Unintended Task Execution and Start Suppression
candidates.abstract: A robot should act only on an instruction from a person or on an intent that the robot explicitly represents and generates. Unintended actions taken without such an instruction can cause risk or inconvenience to people and the environment. We examine how recent vision-language-action (VLA) policies respond when the instruction is missing or meaningless. We apply a paired protocol with empty, neutral, nonsense, infeasible, and wrong-task instructions to six model checkpoints in LIBERO-Goal simulation. Holding the initial state fixed and varying only the instruction, we ask three questions: whether the robot starts to move, which task it completes, and what the instruction determines. Even when the instruction was empty, the robot started moving in every episode with all six checkpoints, and with five of them it often completed a task that the instruction had not specified. On two GR00T checkpoints, the instruction determined which task was executed but not whether the robot started moving; the robot moved even on infeasible instructions. We then tested three methods for suppressing the start: prepending "if no task is given do not move" to the instruction; a gate that holds the robot when the first action chunk for the given instruction nearly equals that for an empty instruction; and fine-tuning the policy to hold still on non-task inputs. The prefix stopped the robot in none of the six checkpoints, and the gate held it on non-task inputs in five of the six checkpoints. The fine-tuned policy never completed a task on non-task inputs, but it did not reliably keep the robot still, and it failed to suppress the start on infeasible instructions.

candidates.title: Chronos-2: A foundation model for multivariate time series forecasting
candidates.abstract: Accurate forecasting with uncertainty quantification is critical in a variety of scientific applications ranging from epidemiology and economics to energy systems and earth sciences. Yet most forecasting models still need to be developed and trained separately for each domain-specific dataset. Time series foundation models (TSFMs) aim to remove this limitation and enable the application of the same model across domains through large-scale pretraining. However, most existing TSFMs treat each time series independently and therefore cannot model interactions among time series and external drivers. Here, we introduce Chronos-2, a foundation model for zero-shot forecasting that models the interactions between multivariate time series and heterogeneous covariates, which commonly arise in scientific applications. The model infers relationships among time series directly from historical context and generates probabilistic forecasts without task-specific treatment. Across various benchmarks, Chronos-2 achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on average by improving skill scores by 5.2 percentage points relative to the strongest baselines and increasing win rates by 10 percentage points. Chronos-2 is also computationally efficient, generating forecasts for 100 time series in under one second on a single mid-range GPU, 50x and 1000x faster end-to-end than the best task-specific point and probabilistic forecasters, respectively. In addition, we demonstrate its effectiveness in diverse scientific settings -- including infectious-disease forecasting, macroeconomic modeling, carbon-flux prediction, and runoff simulation -- where the model matches or surpasses specialized methods developed for each domain. These results show that a single pretrained model can capture structure shared across temporal systems.

candidates.title: Hierarchical World Models with Implicit Dynamics
candidates.abstract: Planning with world models enables test-time adaptation for embodied agents, offering superior generalization over direct policy learning. However, long-horizon tasks remain hindered by cumulative errors and search complexity. Existing hierarchical methods often use rigid macro-actions or latent skills, leading to brittle representations and limited fine-grained control. We introduce ID-WM (Implicit Dynamics World Models), a hierarchical world model that decouples state-space reachability from local control. Our framework utilizes a high-level model to sample feasible transitions across the state manifold and a low-level world model as an inverse dynamics solver to ground these transitions into precise actions. This allows the planner to identify reachable subgoals without being constrained by low-level execution details. By prioritizing local physical feasibility over global behavioral patterns, ID-WM synthesizes novel long-horizon plans from short segments, transcending the specific behavioral modes seen during training. We demonstrate its effectiveness across three navigation and manipulation suites, achieving a 38.5% improvement over state-of-the-art policy and diffusion-based planners. Crucially, by leveraging this hierarchical structure to mitigate compounding errors, our approach yields a 135% performance gain over single-level world model MPC, particularly in complex, unseen configurations for long-horizon tasks. Videos can be viewed at https://id-wm.github.io

candidates.title: "Shall We Approve?" Consequence-Aware Approval for Autonomous Coding Agents
candidates.abstract: Coding agents increasingly rely on automated approvers to decide whether a proposed shell command may run. Existing approvers, from rule-based checkers to guardrail models and deployed permission classifiers, base their decisions on the text of the request and command. Yet a command's behavior depends on the code it invokes and the state of the workspace, and systems that observe file changes leave the assessment to the agent or a human after execution. We present Caper, a consequence-aware approval mechanism that pre-executes each command in a snapshotted sandbox, provides an independent approver with a bounded report of its observed effects, commits allowed commands, and rolls back blocked ones with a reason the agent can act on. Compared with six existing systems, Caper achieves the lowest harmful-outcome rate on SABER (6.7% versus at least 14.8%) and YoloFS-Ext, a benchmark we build in which harmful behavior is hidden inside invoked tools (7.8% versus at least 35.3%), while blocking 1.0% of the safe twins of the dangerous tasks in YoloFS-Ext.

candidates.title: What We Keep of What We Forget: Replacement Operators and Routing Semantics in Training-Free MoE Expert Pruning
candidates.abstract: Training-free expert pruning makes two decisions: which experts to remove, and what the layer computes when its router still selects a removed expert. Published methods change both at once. Holding the mask fixed, we compare replacement operators from three families on OLMoE, DeepSeek-V2-Lite and Moonlight, with Granite as a fourth router, using paired, multiplicity-corrected tests. The largest effect is a choice usually left implicit: the survivors' gate scale. On routers trained without top-k renormalization, renormalizing the survivors' gates, a common implementation choice, costs 0.8-8.5 points and reverses whether rerouting beats MoNE's mean-output replacement; on two routers trained with renormalization, the trained scale wins at 50% pruning. We introduce the tilted novice, a closed-form low-rank map of the pruned expert's input whose rank-0 case is MoNE's constant. At 50% pruning it adds 1.2-1.8% parameters and gains 3.45 and 1.37 points over the constant on OLMoE and Moonlight, stable across calibration draws and largely unchanged by 4- and 3-bit quantization. No operator dominates: trained-scale rerouting is best on DeepSeek-V2-Lite, and a partial copy of each pruned expert is statistically indistinguishable from the tilted novice on two models. Evaluation can change conclusions: at 25% pruning MoNE's constant keeps 92-97% of dense multiple-choice accuracy but only 5-65% of GSM8K and 0-17% of code scores, and the calibration domain moves the mask 4-9 times more than resampling. We propose a five-item reporting checklist.

candidates.title: Anomalies as Residuals: Cauchy Displacement Networks
candidates.abstract: Neighbourhood-based detectors such as KNN, LOF and LUNAR remain among the most accurate methods for tabular anomaly detection, but they compare every query with the stored training set, so their inference cost and memory grow with the data and the data must be kept at deployment. We ask whether the neighbourhood geometry these detectors exploit can be compiled into a small network that scores a query with a single forward pass. We propose the Cauchy Displacement Network (CDN), which regresses each normal point onto the mean of its $k$ nearest training neighbours with a single-hidden-layer network of Cauchy activations and scores a query by the length of its predicted displacement. This displacement is an empirical mean-shift vector, whose fixed-radius population counterpart locally approximates a scaled gradient of the log density. We show that Cauchy units exactly represent the score fields of a structured family of Student-$t$ expert densities, and establish a constructive approximation bound for the corresponding population neighbourhood-mean map using a single-hidden-layer Cauchy network. We further show that the bounded network output guarantees asymptotically linear residual-score growth along every fixed direction. On 46 benchmark datasets against 28 baselines, CDN obtains the best mean rank under both AUC-ROC and AUC-PR, while scoring $10^4$ queries in a few milliseconds on a single CPU thread, up to three orders of magnitude faster than neighbourhood-based detectors, with a model whose size does not depend on the training set.

candidates.title: GraphTFactor: A graph-based approach for proteins transcription factor prediction
candidates.abstract: Transcription factors (TFs) play an important role in regulating gene expression, making their identification a fundamental task in computational biology. In this work, we propose GraphTFactor, a novel end-to-end framework that models protein sequences as graphs and directly classifies transcription factors. By encoding sequences into graph structures, the proposed approach naturally handles variable-length inputs while preserving relevant relational information, without imposing length constraints. Experimental results show that GraphTFactor outperforms state-of-the-art methods on benchmark datasets, demonstrating the effectiveness of graph-based representations for TF prediction while providing interpretable insights into the sequence regions contributing to the model's predictions. To support reproducibility and practical adoption, we release an open-source software package and an interactive web application that let users easily perform TF prediction on custom sequences.

candidates.title: DAPS: Dependency-Aware Premise Selection for LLM Theorem Proving
candidates.abstract: LLM-based theorem proving in Lean 4 has advanced rapidly, but provers are difficult to leverage newly contributed lemmas, because retrieval skews toward popular foundational lemmas, leaving the right premises buried among hundreds of thousands of candidates. Existing neural selectors rank candidates by semantic similarity, with three intrinsic limitations: frequency-skewed retrieval, isolated pairwise ranking, and degradation on out-of-distribution queries such as competition problems and informal language. Given that mathematics is structured by dependencies rather than similarities, we restore this signal to both the training data and the model. We curate two underused dependency resources. We conduct the first systematic mining of 53 Lean Blueprint projects, a previously untapped corpus of 3,805 manually curated informal+formal nodes that capture rare, research-level premises absent from Mathlib4. We further pair it with the extraction of comprehensive, typed, multi-level Mathlib4 dependencies. We then introduce DAPS, a dependency-aware premise selector with a structural neighborhood encoder, a group-level contrastive objective, and a Mathlib-then-Blueprint adaptation procedure. DAPS reaches mean Recall@32 of 89.25 on Mathlib4-Heldout (+11.41 over the strong selector LeanHammer), and maintains this lead on two out-of-distribution benchmarks. Further experiments demonstrate that DAPS premises improve theorem proving on miniF2F and IMO-ProofBench. Project page: https://daps-eth.github.io/.

candidates.title: CalibCause: A Quality-Gated, Interpretable and Calibrated Deep Learning Framework for Diabetic Retinopathy Grading
candidates.abstract: Most deep learning systems for diabetic retinopathy (DR) grading are evaluated on a single data source, with limited evidence of cross-site generalisation, uncertainty calibration, and interpretability. We propose CalibCause, a quality-gated mixture-of-experts framework that combines per-expert visual explanations, label-free image-quality conditioning, knowledge distillation, and calibrated confidence with deferral. We evaluated the framework using 51,310 fundus images from EyePACS, DDR, and APTOS 2019, with IDRiD and DeepDRiD for external testing. Evaluation included pooled testing, leave-one-environment-out experiments, paired bootstrap confidence intervals, and local grade-threshold adaptation. On the pooled test split, the label-free distilled student achieved quadratic weighted kappa (QWK) of 0.863 and accuracy of 0.865 with 27.8 million parameters, 52% fewer than its teacher. Across held-out environments, the label-free model achieved mean QWK of 0.741 compared with 0.743 for a plain ConvNeXt-Tiny baseline, while adversarial invariance did not improve cross-site grading accuracy. Refitting grade thresholds using 200 labelled images increased held-out EyePACS QWK from 0.533 to 0.621 for the label-free model. After vector scaling, expected calibration error ranged from 0.025 to 0.036 across CalibCause variants, and deferring the least confident 20% of images increased student accuracy from 0.865 to 0.923 on the remaining images. These findings demonstrate that quality-aware grading, interpretable expert routing, model compression, and calibrated deferral can be integrated without sacrificing cross-site performance relative to a plain baseline, although reliable deployment still requires local validation and adaptation.

candidates.title: Automatic Construction of Strong Simple Baselines
candidates.abstract: To rigorously establish the value of a novel deep learning method, it must be compared against appropriate baselines. As deep learning has become increasingly common in the physical and life sciences, there have been numerous cases in which apparent progress has turned out to be an artifact of omitted or missing baselines. In this work, we investigate whether this problem can be mitigated by using large language models to automate the construction of baselines. We assemble 36 supervised classification and regression tasks from peer-reviewed studies in Nature, Science, and Cell-family journals that investigate novel deep learning methods for scientific applications. We then use a language model to construct simple baselines for each task. These automatically constructed baselines are strong, recovering a median of 95.5% (mean 85.7%) of the gap between a trivial predictor and the score of the deep learning model. The median simple baseline matches or exceeds the performance of the deep learning model in 12 studies. We further examine the variation across scientific domains and publication venues and we characterize the effects of test-time compute and access to different levels of study context. As human peer review has struggled to keep up with the rapidly increasing volume of research articles in recent years, our results suggest that automated baseline construction is a practical and scalable check on deep learning contributions in the physical and life sciences.

candidates.title: Bayesian Distribution System State Estimation with Flow Matching
candidates.abstract: Medium-voltage feeders have few real-time measurements, so distribution system state estimation (DSSE) rests on pseudo-measurements of the secondary substations, a prior in Bayesian terms. Weighted least squares keeps the power flow exact but reduces this prior to a mean and variance, while supervised deep learning estimators also learn the power flow and are tied to one measurement set. We propose PoSE (posterior sampling for state estimation), which keeps the Bayesian structure of DSSE and learns only what the distribution system operator does not know, namely the distribution of substation injections, modelled by a neural network trained with flow matching on historical data. The power flow equations, grid topology and measurements enter only at sampling, through a noise-aware Kalman-type correction. The neural network therefore never approximates the power flow, but every posterior sample is a physically consistent operating point, and one trained prior serves any measurement set, noise level and topology. On the IEEE 33-bus feeder, PoSE lowers the probabilistic injection error (CRPS) by 6.7-7.5% against a full-covariance Gaussian prior in all 12 tested settings. It provides reliable uncertainty: the 90% intervals contain the true injection almost exactly as often as exact posterior samples would, whereas those of supervised estimators contain it in only 37-78% of cases. On the 240-bus unbalanced three-phase Iowa feeder, it gives the lowest injection, voltage and branch-current errors of all estimators. A fast variant matches this accuracy at 0.2-0.6s per snapshot and, without retraining, beats Gaussian priors and retrained supervised estimators on seven reconfigured topologies.

candidates.title: Don't Just Impute, Detect: Task-Aware Diffusion Pipelines for Edge Anomaly Detection
candidates.abstract: Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) edge pipelines routinely lose contiguous blocks of multi-sensor data to network dropouts and hardware faults. The standard remedy is a disjointed "impute-then-detect" pipeline whose imputer is trained only for Mean Squared Error (MSE). Such an imputer fills a missing block with the most probable normal pattern: a partially observed anomaly is smoothed back toward normality, and boundary artifacts on normal data raise false alarms. We call this imputation bias and propose the Task-Aware Diffusion Refiner (TADR), a conditional diffusion refiner trained against the loss landscape of a frozen downstream detector. Because back-propagating through the sampling trajectory is intractable, the task-aware terms act on the one-step clean-window estimate that the noise prediction already yields, so training costs no more than plain diffusion training. Under strict Point-to-Point evaluation over five seeds with paired significance tests, TADR raises F1 by $0.338$ over the unrefined detector on SMD ($p = 0.0015$), and the anomaly enhancement objective alone contributes $0.463$ in ablation. We also characterise when the method helps: the gain tracks the continuous, mutually redundant channels available and the anomaly evidence the outage removes, and it is absent on telemetry datasets dominated by one-hot command channels and on PSM. At ten sampling steps TADR runs in $41.4$ ms per window on a single CPU core, sustaining about $24$ concurrent 1 Hz streams from a $4.03$ MB model. Code and per-seed results are available at https://github.com/int-park422/TADR.

candidates.title: Completeness and dynamical stability in exoplanet occurrence rates
candidates.abstract: Exoplanet population studies are often quantified through the "occurrence rate" of certain types of planet. This value can be calculated from a survey of a sample of stars by taking the "detection rate" and correcting with a completeness factor. This completeness is calculated via detection limits on each individual star, and can be calculated either individually for each detected planet or averaged in a certain area of parameter space. We test whether either the average completeness or individual completeness performs better than the other. We also test whether including dynamical stability constraints in the detection limits improves the occurrence rate results. We use synthetic sets of exoplanetary systems and calculate occurrence rates for each and compare to what the value would be with perfect information. We compare how close each method is to the ground truth to assess which is most suitable. Overall, in our synthetic sets, the average completeness is more reliable though it can be a problem if there is a sharp change in the underlying population within the area of parameter-space considered. We find that using dynamical stability conditions causes a bias in the occurrence rate and do not recommend using these.

candidates.title: An end-to-end CNN search for ultra-short-period planets in TESS: from the blend ceiling to the independent validation of TOI-6662 b
candidates.abstract:
We trained a convolutional neural network to detect ultra-short-period planets in TESS photometry, following the procedure now standard in the field: synthetic transits as positives, eclipsing binaries as negatives. Measured that way it reaches an area under the ROC curve of 0.97. Keeping the same model and the same planets, but replacing the negatives with false positives that the TESS Follow-up Observing Program has actually rejected, the area falls to 0.50 -- the value of a random classifier. The conventional benchmark had been measuring a problem that does not exist.
  The reason is physical, and it bounds what is possible. Of 145 such false positives examined at pixel level, 42% are blends: eclipses belonging to a neighbouring star, diluted into the target aperture. Their light curves are indistinguishable from shallow transits, capping the attainable area at 1 - f/2 = 0.79. Retraining on real false positives reaches 0.80 +/- 0.06, confirming the ceiling independently. No classifier reading a single-band light curve can do better.
  A detector alone is the wrong instrument. We built CASCADE-USP, a pipeline chaining the network with difference-image centroid analysis, scene modelling with high-resolution imaging and the Gaia astrometric solution, supplying in sequence what the light curve lacks. Its output is a prioritisation, not a verdict: it records what evidence each candidate still needs. Only the classifier is domain-specific; the other stages apply to any transit candidate. Of 435 unresolved TESS candidates it isolates 20; 19 prove false positives, traced to causes invisible in TESS photometry. The twentieth is TOI-6662 b, an Earth-sized planet (0.94 +/- 0.03 Earth radii) orbiting an M dwarf every 7.05 hours. Our validation, independent of a concurrent one, agrees with it in planetary parameters and classification, closing the CASCADE procedure with an external check.

candidates.title: From Anoxic to Oxic Earth: Detectability of Atmospheric Biosignatures across Stellar Hosts with ELT/ANDES
candidates.abstract: Earth's atmosphere evolved from an anoxic, methane-bearing Archean state through Proterozoic oxygenation to the O$_2$-rich modern atmosphere. However, most biosignature detectability studies focus on modern Earth, leaving earlier atmospheric states comparatively unexplored. We investigate how atmospheric evolution and stellar environments influence the detectability of O$_2$, CH$_4$, H$_2$O, and CO$_2$, and their potential to distinguish anoxic from oxygenated atmospheres. We construct two complementary photochemical grids: representative Archean, Proterozoic, and modern-Earth scenarios around the Sun, and four geological epochs (3.9, 2.0, 0.8 Ga, and modern Earth) across FGKM hosts. Combining one-dimensional photochemical modeling, high-resolution transmission spectral simulations, and instrument-noise modeling, we assess molecular detectability with ELT/ANDES under optimistic photon-noise-limited conditions. For solar-host Archean and Proterozoic models, CH$_4$ requires approximately 33 and 42 transits, respectively, to reach the adopted 5$\sigma$ criterion, whereas O$_2$ remains below 3$\sigma$ within the observing limits. Modern-Earth O$_2$ reaches 3$\sigma$ after approximately 38 transits. Across the FGKM grid, O$_2$ does not reach 5$\sigma$ for the 3.9 Ga models. However, For the M3V, K2V, and M8V proxies, modern-Earth O$_2$ reaches 5$\sigma$ in 9, 15, and 20 transits, respectively, whereas CH$_4$ requires 11, 12, and 28 transits at 3.9 Ga and only 2--4 transits across the oxygenated epochs. These results reveal a strong O$_2$ detectability contrast around M and K-dwarfs, but not Sun-like hosts in the YJH bands. Robust biosignature interpretation requires complementary molecular constraints, including informative non-detections, within the context of atmospheric evolution and stellar environment.

candidates.title: Distinguishing N$_2$-Dominated from O$_2$-Dominated Atmospheres on Terrestrial Exoplanets with Reflected-Light Spectroscopy
candidates.abstract: Reflected-light spectra of Earth-sized exoplanets promise to probe habitability and biosignatures, but interpreting atmospheric oxygen can be challenging because $O_2$ can arise from both biological and abiotic processes. In addition, reflected-light retrievals exhibit degeneracies among atmospheric composition, clouds, surface reflectance, and gravity. We use the Bayesian retrieval framework ExoReL$^\Re$, leveraging recent model developments that incorporate (i) $O_2$-$O_2$ collision-induced absorption (CIA), which produces the $O_4$ bands, and (ii) a wavelength-dependent (step-function) surface albedo parameterization. Focusing on a modern Earth analog, we compare retrievals with and without $O_2$-$O_2$ CIA using spectra within 0.25-1.8 $\mu$m, and perform signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) sweeps for two observing configurations motivated by the Habitable Worlds Observatory: a resolved-visible case ($R_{VIS}=140$) and a broadband-visible case (three broad bins). Omitting $O_2$-$O_2$ CIA allows the retrieval to fit the spectrum with an incorrect $O_2$-dominated atmosphere. Including $O_2$-$O_2$ CIA leverages the $O_4$ bands to break this degeneracy and recover the correct $N_2$-dominated, $O_2$-rich solution without requiring a tight mass prior. Adopting a robustness criterion of $\ge95\%$ posterior mass in the $N_2$-dominated region, both configurations require SNR $\gtrsim20$ at 0.75 $\mu$m (SNR $\approx14$ near the 1.27 $\mu$m $O_4$ band for $R_{NIR}=70$) to identify the correct dominant gas, with higher cloud fraction increasing this threshold. Reducing near-IR coverage to 1.4 $\mu$m prevents recovery of the correct $N_2$-dominated solution across the explored SNR range, and instead favors a spurious $O_2$-dominated, $CO_2$-rich atmosphere. These results support near-IR coverage to $\sim1.7$ $\mu$m and SNR $\gtrsim20$ at 0.75 $\mu$m for robust oxygen interpretation on Earth-like planets.

candidates.title: Likely Metal Scarring in the Magnetic White Dwarf LHS 2534
candidates.abstract: There are only three white dwarfs known to possess metal-enriched polar caps due to magnetically guided accretion. These rare systems offer a unique opportunity to study planetesimal accretion and how magnetic fields influence the spreading of material across the atmosphere. To better study these processes however, more targets are needed. Here we report our findings from an observing campaign on the magnetic white dwarf LHS 2534. Time-resolved spectra at the MMT show clear variability in the strength of the Na I and Cr I features. We find that the strengths of these features vary over a period of 19.46 and 19.36 hours respectively, closely matching the 20.22 hour period determined from K2 photometry. Our findings demonstrate the ability to detect and study these variable objects with spectroscopy, and time-series observations of similar targets in the future will provide more insight into how these atmospheres form.

candidates.title: Current Sheets and Magnetic Reconnection statistics by Solar Orbiter at few to tens of Ion Inertial Lengths I: Energy Dissipation
candidates.abstract: In this work, we study the turbulent origin of ion-scale Current Sheets (CSs) and the dissipation of energy via magnetic reconnection. We analyze 103 hours of high-cadence (4 samples/s) in-situ ion data from Solar Orbiter, collected between July 2020 and September 2022. We apply an automatic detection algorithm that finds current sheets (CSs) of thickness (length in the normal direction, $\lambda$) near the ion inertial length ($\delta_i$), and classifies them as Alfv\'enic or reconnecting. We compile a catalog of 974 CSs of thickness in the range of few to 90 ion inertial lengths, of which 53 contain an ion reconnection jet. We estimate that Solar Orbiter spends $\sim 1 \%$ of the dwell time inside a CS of few to 90 $\delta_i$ thickness, and 0.06\% inside a reconnecting CS of the same thickness range. By comparing these results with previous studies we estimate that the abundance of CSs and of Reconnecting CSs evolves with heliocentric distance ($r$) as $r^{-0.9}$ and $r^{-1.5}$, respectively. We estimate that magnetic reconnection dissipates $\epsilon_{rec}\sim 30 \hspace{5pt} \text{J} \text{kg}^{-1} \text{s}^{-1},$ in the $\sim 1 - 40$ $\delta_i$ scale-range, by assessing the amount of plasma that interacts with a reconnection exhaust. We show how the dissipation of turbulence energy cascade by magnetic reconnection at scales smaller than 90 $\delta_i$ is more effective closer to the Sun, and decays as $r^{-3.6}$. The current density of Alfv\'enic CSs thicker than the ion inertial length presents scale invariance, obeying $J_0/J_A=0.9(\lambda/2\delta_i)^{-0.71}$, suggesting that CSs generated locally from solar wind turbulence.
authors: V\'ictor Montagud-Camps (Universitat de les Illes Balears
Na\"is Fargette (Institut de Recherche en Astrophysique et Plan\'etologie)
Beno\^it Lavraud (Institut de Recherche en Astrophysique et Plan\'etologie
Philippe Louarn (Institut de Recherche en Astrophysique et Plan\'etologie)

candidates.title: Formation of Micron-sized Presolar Graphite Grains in Low-energy Supernova Ejecta
candidates.abstract: Presolar graphite grains with supernova isotopic signatures provide direct evidence that large graphite grains formed in supernova ejecta. However, theoretical calculations of dust formation in supernovae have typically predicted graphite grains smaller than $0.1\,{\rm \mu m}$, leaving unclear the physical conditions required to form those grains with radii of order $1\,{\rm \mu m}$. We systematically investigate graphite nucleation and growth in expanding supernova ejecta by varying the explosion energy, ejecta mass, initial ejecta radius, and ejected $^{56}$Ni mass. We use a simplified one-zone model that follows the temperature and density evolution including adiabatic cooling, radiative cooling, and heating by radioactive nickel. We show that the final graphite grain size is mainly determined by the product of the mass density of atomic carbon available for grain growth and the local cooling timescale, both evaluated at a reference temperature of $2000\,{\rm K}$. Our models show that graphite growth is favored by lower explosion energy, larger ejecta mass, and smaller initial ejecta radius, which keep the gas denser near the graphite-condensation temperature. When radioactive heating and radiative cooling are included, explosions with $E_{\rm exp}\sim10^{50}\,{\rm erg}$ and $M_{\rm Ni}\lesssim10^{-3}\,M_\odot$ can form $1$-$10\,\mu{\rm m}$ graphite grains in the ejected helium layer or carbon-oxygen core, whereas $E_{\rm exp}\sim10^{51}\,{\rm erg}$ models do not. These results suggest that micron-sized presolar supernova graphite preferentially forms in faint-supernova-like explosions with low explosion energies, little ejected nickel, and helium layer or carbon-oxygen core ejecta.

candidates.title: Agentic Systems for Calibrating Cosmological Simulations
candidates.abstract: Calibrating a cosmological simulation is an expensive, high-dimensional parameter optimization task. Previous works employ Bayesian optimization for automation, which treats the simulator as a black box and precludes the incorporation of human domain knowledge or workflow into the selection policy. We propose AgenticTuner, an agentic calibration pipeline with a present-day large language model serving as the optimizer who proposes the next parameter trial. We show that these agents can achieve competitive calibration performance at a fraction of the CPU cost when they are given informal, human-readable priors (such as codebase, documentation, and heuristic guides that seasoned scientists may possess). We hope this work serves as an early step toward AI scientists that can carry out complex, long-horizon scientific tasks.

candidates.title: Machine Learning Sensor Fusion for Water Vapor Radiometry based Tropospheric Delay Calibration
candidates.abstract: The next-generation Very Large Array (ngVLA) intends to use 22 GHz water vapor radiometry (WVR) to correct for tropospheric phase fluctuations in its high-frequency bands. However, current delay-retrieval methods do not reach the required accuracy and reliability. As a remedy, we propose a machine-learning based retrieval concept and a preliminary architecture, framed as heterogeneous, multi-rate sensor fusion. Atmospheric reanalysis profiles and surface weather set the context in which per-antenna WVR spectra are used to estimate excess path by a Kalman filter whose parameters are learned from high-cadence calibrator phases. The method is being developed, with planned first validation on the 183 GHz WVR system of the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA).

candidates.title: An Assessment of Water Vapor Radiometry Landscape in ngVLA Context
candidates.abstract: The ngVLA intends to utilize Water Vapor Radiometry (WVR) as an approach to lower calibration overheads for tropospheric phase fluctuation correction in its high frequency bands (5 \& 6; 30.5-116 GHz) to levels below those feasible with fast switched reference gain calibration. As a stepping stone to an eventual ngVLA WVR system, the JVLA/ngVLA teams pursued an effort to develop and install a set of MMIC based compact water vapor radiometers (CWVR) and carry out on-sky testing. Most recent tests found that the CWVRs installed on the VLA antennas under this effort were non-functional in tracking visibility phases. As part of the program to develop a WVR system for the ngVLA, this memo summarizes the current landscape of water vapor radiometry experience, the situation with the CWVRs, how they relate to the ngVLA WVR requirements, and the work needed to operationalize the CWVRs as useful test systems and to make broader progress. We currently lack statistically relevant WVR correction data to understand their expected performance for the ngVLA sites. We also discuss parallel additional approaches alternative and/or complementary to the CWVRs. A path involving tests to establish the functionality, stability, sensitivity, and switched power cal/data synchronism of the CWVR system in the lab and on antenna, followed by on-sky tests, and a parallel effort to assess the utility of autocorrelation outputs of the VLA K-band receivers for delay estimation is recommended. Potential paths going beyond traditional excess path estimation methods which may be necessary to meet ngVLA requirements and goals are touched upon.

candidates.title: Spectral Information Content of Diffraction-Limited Images
candidates.abstract: High-resolution optical imaging is fundamentally limited by diffraction, which imprints wavelength-dependent structure onto the point spread function (PSF) of the optical system. This intrinsic chromaticity implies that in addition to spatial structure, images encode spectral information. We develop the theory of this spectral information content and provide strategies for its optimal extraction with calculations of Fisher information. We show that polychromatic PSF formation can be expressed as a convolution in logarithmic coordinates and define the corresponding spectral transfer function. We derive this function for the Airy disk and find algebraic decay in spectral log-frequency, implying the existence of arbitrarily fine spectral structure in the ideal, noiseless PSF. We use a differentiable forward model to numerically construct the spectral information eigenbasis and quantify the spectroscopic capability of diffraction-limited imaging across a range of noise and detector systematics. We demonstrate injection and recovery of the constrained spectral modes in a realistic simulated example and compare these results with previously reported methods. Our information-theoretic framework provides a generalisable method for spectral characterisation of PSFs spanning a variety of imaging contexts.

candidates.title: Cryogenic Optical Characteristics of S-FPL51 and S-LAH71: Refractive index, Transmission and Thermal expansion
candidates.abstract:
Several near-infrared instruments on upcoming extremely large telescopes use a combination of OHARA S-FPL51 and S-LAH71 glass prisms to correct for the atmospheric differential refraction. Because large parts of these instruments are contained within a vessel cooled to liquid nitrogen temperatures, the changes in optical and mechanical properties should be considered during the design phase.
  In this report, we provide an update to our continuing efforts to characterize the S-FPL51 and S-LAH71 glass under cryogenic conditions. These efforts include a measurement of the refractive index (293 K, 100 K and 80 K), transmission measurements (293 K, 77 K and 43 K) and a determination of the coefficient of thermal expansion (between 293 K and 45 K). We will describe the cryogenic test setups that we have used to obtain our results, and provide summarizing equations of these material properties.
  This characterization will prove useful for conceptual design trade-offs, mechanical interface solutions and detailed optical design for future near-infrared instrumentation on large telescopes.

candidates.title: Demographics and growth of the astronomy and astrophysics community
candidates.abstract: This paper presents the demographics and growth of the astronomy and astrophysics community over the past ~200 years based on data provided by the Astrophysics Data System. The analysis suggests that 59940 authors signed at least one paper in 2025, while about 40% of the community did not publish any papers, resulting in an estimated community size of roughly 100000 astronomers in 2025. About 38% of the community is hosted in Europe, followed by Asia (29%), North America (26%), South America (4%), Oceania (2%) and Africa (1%). Large variations exist among the countries in the number of astronomers, astronomers per capita of country population and astronomers per country gross domestic product (GDP). Overall, the community is dominated by early career scientists, with 50% of the authors publishing papers for seven years or less. This dominance is readily explained by a steady and exponential growth of the community of 4.3% per year over the last 50 years, implying that the community-size doubled every 16 years. The growth rate of the community exceeds that of the number of papers or paper pages, implying that the annual number of papers or pages published per astronomer is on decline. Over the last decade, the exponential growth of the community has accelerated to 5.1% per year, owing in particular to countries like China (13% per year) and India (10% per year). For almost all countries in the world, growth rates in authors, authors per capita and authors per GDP are positive. The growth in astronomy is not an exception, as the growth rates of the earth sciences and physics communities are even larger. If the past tendencies continue, Chinese and Indian astronomers will be first and second largest communities in the world by 2029 and 2043, respectively.

candidates.title: HWP-synchronous signal induced by misalignment of the sapphire crystal axis
candidates.abstract: We investigate the optical response of a rotating sapphire half-wave plate (HWP) with optic axis misalignment, defined as a deviation of the optic axis from the ideal a-cut orientation. We extend the transfer-matrix formalism for calculating the modulated transmittance of multi-layer wave plates with optic axis misalignment and oblique incidence. Using this formalism, we compute the modulated response of a rotating HWP with an optic axis misalignment to linearly polarized incident light. We experimentally validate the model at 90 GHz using sapphire wave plates with intentionally introduced optic axis misalignments of up to 30 degrees. Additional even harmonics are observed for oblique incidence and optic axis misalignment, with odd harmonics appearing when both effects are present. The measured modulation signals are in good agreement with the model predictions. We also evaluate the potential impact of a illustrative small optic axis misalignment of 3 degrees on precision polarimetry. For the configuration considered, the model predicts odd-harmonic amplitudes at the percent level for a single-layer HWP and up to 8% at individual frequencies for a five-layer achromatic HWP.

candidates.title: First Light with the Dark100 Array of PANOSETI Telescopes at Palomar Observatory
candidates.abstract: Dark100 is the first phase of an extensive array of Panoramic SETI (PANOSETI) telescopes at Palomar Observatory, California. PANOSETI telescopes are small, 0.5-m Fresnel lens telescopes instrumented with 1024-pixel silicon photomultiplier (SiPM) cameras. The telescopes were originally designed to search for ultra-fast optical transients, but they also function as cost-effective imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes (IACTs). Dark100 will use seven of these widely separated IACTs to map the ultra-high-energy (UHE) gamma-ray sources on the Galactic Plane at high resolution. Dark100 will also leverage the IACT technique to search for evidence of ultra-heavy dark matter in a mass range that extends beyond 100 TeV. Deployment of the first four telescopes and enclosures was completed in December 2025, and commissioning of the next three is scheduled to finish by the end of 2026.
